biopalm.answer: SETTLED. BioPalm Energy Limited is a company incorporated in SINGAPORE, Singapore company registration number 201007394Z. The source is Equatorial Palm Oil plc's own shareholder circular of 10 December 2010 ('Proposals relating to the Restructuring and Financing of the Company's Liberian Palm Oil Projects / Notice of General Meeting'), which defines BioPalm in its Definitions section and describes it again in Part I. The circular gives NO street address for BioPalm, only the jurisdiction of incorporation, so the map can justify a Singapore marker at country/city level but has no documentary street address. The circular separately confirms the card's existing description: BioPalm is a wholly owned subsidiary of Siva Ventures, and the Siva Group is Chennai-based. The card's 'Singapore' headquarters is therefore CORRECT and now sourced, where before it was not.

cobrac.answer: PARTLY SETTLED, and it CONTRADICTS the card. (a) COBRAC's own corporate seat: NO SOURCE FOUND. Four academic sources on the Santo Amaro contamination were opened in full (Ambiente & Sociedade article on SciELO, the same article's Redalyc PDF, and a UNILAB monograph) and none states a headquarters or 'sede' for Companhia Brasileira de Chumbo - they give only the plant site at Santo Amaro, Bahia. RECOMMENDATION: drop the headquarters line as currently written. (b) 'Rieux, France' has NO documentary support whatsoever as a corporate seat for either COBRAC or Peñarroya. Nothing in any source opened mentions Rieux in connection with either company; a targeted search for a Peñarroya site at Rieux returned nothing connecting the two. The 'Rieux' line should be removed, not relocated. (c) The PARENT's seat IS documented, in two periods and two different places, so if the card names the parent it must date the address: Peñarroya was a French company with a Paris office at 12, place Vendôme (documented 1930 and 1951); by the end of the COBRAC period the same legal entity had been renamed Metaleurop SA and the European Commission's 1990 decision gives its address as 118 Péripole, 44 rue Roger Salengro, 94126 Fontenay-sous-Bois, France. (d) New context bearing on the card: a UNILAB monograph states that in 1987 control of COBRAC was acquired by Companhia Adubos Trevo of Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, together with Companhia Paulista de Metais, and that in 1989 the company was incorporated into Plumbum Mineração e Metalurgia. So for its last six years COBRAC was not Peñarroya-controlled at all - naming a French parent as the company's base for the whole 1960-1993 span would be wrong.

French searches for Société Minière et Métallurgique de Peñarroya siège social; opened the Annales des Mines history of the company (which covers its Brazilian operations from 1950 and the 1973 buy-out of its American partners at Boquira, Bahia, but gives no seat and never mentions Santo Amaro or COBRAC), two entreprises-coloniales.fr archival compilations, and the 1990 European Commission decision. Searched specifically for any Peñarroya connection to Rieux, France: nothing. TWO HOSTS REFUSED (bot protection, Anubis 'Access Denied' pages, not permission denials): recherche-anmt.culture.gouv.fr (French national business archives) and pm20.zbw.eu (ZBW press archive) - both are worth a retry by another route, as the ANMT holds the Peñarroya company fonds and would likely state the siège social for the 1960s-80s. The USGS Minerals Yearbook text on search.library.wisc.edu returned a 'Browser not allowed' page.

alcoa.answer: SETTLED for Alcoa Corporation, and it CONFIRMS the card (Pittsburgh), while dating the New York address to 2016-2017 only. Alcoa Corporation (NYSE: AA, the Delaware company separated in November 2016) currently gives its principal executive offices as 201 Isabella Street, Suite 500, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 15212-5858. The move happened during 2017: the FY2016 Form 10-K (first annual report of the new Alcoa Corporation, covering the year ended 31 December 2016) gives 390 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10022-4608, and the FY2017 Form 10-K already gives 201 Isabella Street, Pittsburgh. The same Pittsburgh address appears on the FY2018 and FY2023 10-K covers and on the cover of the proxy statement dated 19 March 2026, whose 'About Alcoa' section also states 'Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA Headquarters'. The 2016 S-1 address of 390 Park Avenue therefore belongs to Alcoa Corporation at separation, not to it now, and not to the old Alcoa Inc. (Note on entity: all four 10-K covers quoted below are Alcoa Corporation's, CIK 1675149, incorporated in Delaware. Nothing here was checked against the old Alcoa Inc., which CIK 4281 covers and which became Arconic.) CAVEAT ON RECENCY: the most recent 10-K I could actually open was FY2023. The FY2024 10-K (accession 0000950170-25-024242, files dated 2025-02-20) and the FY2025 10-K (accession 0001193125-26-077167, per a filing tracker filed 2026-02-26) exist, but I could not open either cover - see 'searched'. The 19 March 2026 proxy statement, an Alcoa SEC filing served from Alcoa's own IR CDN, carries the Pittsburgh address eight months ago and is the best current evidence.

johnson_controls.answer: SETTLED, and it ADDS to the card rather than contradicting it. The cover page of Johnson Controls International plc's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 30 September 2025 gives the principal executive offices as One Albert Quay, Cork, Ireland, T12 X8N6, jurisdiction of incorporation Ireland. So the Cork marker is correct. On the Glendale question: 'Glendale' does NOT appear anywhere in the document. I read the whole 10-K - all 459,000 characters, in five passes at offsets 0, 100000, 200000, 300000 and 400000 - and searched each pass for 'Glendale', 'Milwaukee', 'Wisconsin', 'corporate campus' and 'principal operating office'. 'Glendale' appears zero times; 'corporate campus' and 'principal operating office' appear zero times. 'Milwaukee' appears three times, in these roles: (1) Item 2 Properties, as the company's NORTH AMERICAN OPERATIONAL HEADQUARTERS; (2) Item 3 Legal Proceedings, as a court venue ('Circuit Court for Milwaukee County, Wisconsin'); (3) the independent auditor's signature block location line, 'Milwaukee, Wisconsin'. 'Wisconsin' also appears as the state where Johnson Controls was originally incorporated in 1885 as Johnson Electric Service Company, and extensively in the PFAS litigation and environmental sections in connection with the Marinette, Wisconsin Fire Technology Center and Stanton Street plant. RECOMMENDATION for the card: keep Cork as the registered office and the marker, and add that the company's own 10-K names Milwaukee, Wisconsin as its North American operational headquarters. Do NOT write 'Glendale' or 'corporate campus' - the 10-K supports neither word.

bwdb.answer: SETTLED with a primary source, and the figure matches Banglapedia exactly. The Bangladesh Water Development Board's own 'Achievement at a Glance' series, published on BWDB's own domain (pani.bwdb.gov.bd), gives total embankment length as 10,224 km in its 'UPTO JUNE, 2009' report, under the heading 'ACHIEVEMENT OF MAJOR PHYSICAL COMPONENTS'. The row reads 'a) Embankment 2977 7247 10224 Km' under columns 'Pre-Ind.', 'Post-Ind.', 'Total' - that is, 2,977 km built before independence plus 7,247 km after, totalling 10,224 km, which the document's sub-rows split further into 4,530 km coastal and 5,694 km other. IMPORTANT DATING POINT for the card: the figure is as of JUNE 2009, not as of now. The card can now cite BWDB itself and drop reliance on Banglapedia, but it must carry the June 2009 date. Two caveats worth recording: (1) the document presents the figure in a table, not a sentence, and nowhere uses the word 'cumulative' or 'constructed' next to it, so 'as of June 2009 BWDB reported a total of 10,224 km of embankments' is the safest wording. (2) Other primary sources give different and larger numbers on different definitions, so do not stack them: a BWDB Central GIS Directorate presentation to Sentinel Asia lists completed embankment lengths including a figure of 16,528 km under 'Major Structural Interventions: till date' (its page layout separates the numbers from the category labels, so I could not tie each number to its category and did not try); the Ministry of Finance's Grant No. 44 water-sector medium-term expenditure document reports recent project work of '155.753 km of embankments' constructed and '2673.192 km of embankments' reconstructed; BWDB's own 2013 Resettlement Action Plan for the Coastal Embankment Improvement Project says 'These polders have about 6,000 km of embankments that protect 1.2 million hectares'; and a 2004 World Bank Project Information Document says 'In total, about 9,000 km of embankments have been constructed by the government over the, years', attributing it to the government generally rather than to BWDB.
